correctness.rationale: Incidence-flag counting follows from one-coloured pair per Fano line, forcing colour-class sizes 1,2,4 and collinear singleton/two-class triple. The point-assignment extension table exhausts 3^7 initial assignments; the full graph has 2106 colourings and 6804 legal edges. An incidence argument shows that any proper colouring using all three colours on point vertices is a frozen flag; every colouring using at most two point colours has an explicit integer-height lift. A complete integer-height consistency check independently identifies precisely the 1980 mobile colourings; the 2007 height lemma connects them. Both included standalone programs independently enumerate every state and verify the 126 frozen flags and every mobile state's eccentricity 21; the second also checks the exact L1 lift formula for all 1980^2 ordered pairs. An explicit pair of opposite bipartition-constant colourings has distance 21. General heights and median formula are proved under the stated hypotheses, not assumed from numerical logs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general theorem does imply non-mixing once a frozen colouring is exhibited, and it provides the proof of connectivity for the zero-winding class. It does not determine that exactly 126 colourings have nonzero winding, that they all are frozen and flag-parametrized, that every other colouring is zero-winding, or that the unique mobile component is self-centred with radius/diameter 21. The present result requires those independent finite-geometry steps.

value.rationale: The first (3,6)-cage is a natural extremal cubic bipartite graph where single-site Glauber dynamics is reducible. The exact Fano-flag classification exhausts all frozen traps, while the remainder forms a unique 1980-state sector with sharp, self-centred diameter 21. This explains a complete natural state-space structure and supplies a reproducible benchmark for finite graph-colouring reconfiguration and sampling. The result is not based on value from the raw chromatic count alone.
